doc.title: Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 23, 2003 [interview 2 of 2]

title: An overdubbed melody on a recent record
summary: Listening to a track, Bucky explains he overdubbed the melody, and that the tunesmith brings only a lead sheet.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Let me test your memory here. This is something that you played on, and I wanted to ask you about it. And I just lost it, so see if I can start again. A guy we were talking about earlier.
Okay. Because I wanted to ask you how you did this. I’m going to turn it up here as soon as I find the spot.
Okay. That’s beautiful. Joe always comes up with these interesting little tunes to do.
When he comes up with a song like that, does he bring in a chord chart?
No. He might have a lead sheet.
Lead sheet? Um boy. That’s where the extra string comes in nice, huh?
